title: Guacamole
description: Four ripe avocados, a very finely minced clove of garlic, coriander and lime. Keep it a little lumpy and serve it from the Tupperware so there’s one less bowl to wash.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of chunky guacamole in a dark bowl with tortilla chips on a wooden table.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · guacamole with tomato and chips variation · serving inspiration
personalNote: Mince the garlic as finely as you humanly can. We want it mixed through the guacamole without finding a big lump of raw garlic in a mouthful.
advancePrep: Use ripe avocados. If the Tupperware is big enough, mix straight into it and save washing another bowl.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: Smash, then mince as finely as possible.

steps.title: Make the garlic really fine
steps.description: Smash the garlic clove and mince it as finely as you humanly can. Finely chop the coriander leaves.

steps.title: Mash the avocados
steps.description: Scoop the ripe avocados into the Tupperware and mash them with a fork. If the box is too small for mixing, use a bowl and transfer it afterwards.

steps.title: Mix it all together
steps.description: Add the finely minced garlic, coriander, lime juice and salt. Mix and mash until it is semi-lumpy. We don’t need it completely smooth.
steps.doneness: A little lumpy, with the garlic and herbs mixed through.

steps.title: Serve from the box
steps.description: Serve the guacamole from the Tupperware so we don’t have another bowl to wash. This is enough for two nights; use a clean spoon and put the lid back on before returning what we’re saving to the fridge.

storage: Keep covered in the fridge between dinners and use a clean serving spoon. Put the saved guacamole back in the fridge promptly.
servingSuggestion: Have alongside the tacos, fajitas, enchiladas or a Mexican bowl. This batch is for both nights.
portionNote: The full batch is a side for two dinners for both of us: 4 side portions.
